newsitem.title: ROMANIA: France ready to back Romania bid to join EU, NATO.
newsitem.headline: France ready to back Romania bid to join EU, NATO.

text.p: France is ready to support Romania's ambitious plan to be among the first countries to join the process of NATO and European Union enlargement, a senior French official said on Tuesday.

"France wants Romania to be part of the first wave in the NATO enlargement. I want to reassess France's support for Romania in the process of joining the alliance," European Affairs Minister Michel Barnier Barnier told reporters in Bucharest after meeting Romanian President Emil Constantinescu.
Romania's geographic location and political stability were assets which qualified the Balkan country to join NATO, he said.
"I think Romania will be well prepared to meet NATO requirements for new members, expected to be established at the NATO summit in July," Barnier said.
Barnier said he had also come to Romania to prepare an official visit to Bucharest by French President Jacques Chirac, scheduled for February 20-22.

It will be the first trip by a Western leader to Romania since the elections last November in which Constantinescu ousted ex-communist Ion Iliescu and the country got a reformist government formed by centrist parties.

Chirac's visit was expected to boost ties between the two Francophone states, Barnier said, adding that a newly-created French-Romanian economic commission would seek ways to boost economic cooperation between the two states.
"We were very much impressed by the determination of the government to join the EU. We will help and support Romania on all levels," Barnier said.

Romania, the only East European state with a Latin-based language, has had strong cultural links with France for the past two centuries, an influence which shows in Romanian architecture, art and social manners. Many Romanians consider France an "elder sister".
Romania was the first ex-Warsaw Pact member to join NATO's Partnership for Peace programme.
